description: Labeled eval set for off-plan resale RAG. Each item: question, gold_source (file that should be retrieved), gold_doc_type, reference_answer (for correctness), and answer_keys (substrings a faithful answer should contain).

questions.question: What minimum percentage of the price must an original buyer have paid before a developer approves an off-plan assignment?
questions.reference_answer: Developers typically require 30 to 40 percent of the price to be paid before approving an assignment; some premium projects set the threshold at 50 percent. The exact figure is in the unit's SPA.

questions.question: What is the Oqood re-registration fee for an off-plan resale?
questions.reference_answer: The Oqood re-registration fee is AED 5,000 to 10,000, set by the DLD.

questions.question: What document must the seller obtain from the developer to complete an off-plan resale, and what does it confirm?
questions.reference_answer: A No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the developer. It confirms developer consent to the transfer, that the seller is current on payments, and transfers the remaining payment plan to the new buyer.

questions.question: What is the total transaction cost range for an off-plan resale as a share of sale price?
questions.reference_answer: Total resale transaction cost is typically around 6 to 11 percent of the sale price, combining the 4% DLD fee, Oqood re-registration, developer NOC and assignment fees, and agency commission.

questions.question: What is an off-plan resale legally called and what is actually being transferred?
questions.reference_answer: It is an assignment of contract: the seller assigns their rights and obligations under the Sale and Purchase Agreement (SPA) to a new buyer, who assumes the remaining payment plan. No completed unit or title deed is conveyed yet.

questions.question: Which Dubai law regulates the interim property register for off-plan sales?
questions.reference_answer: Law No. (13) of 2008 Regulating the Interim Property Register in the Emirate of Dubai.

questions.question: In the interim property register law, what happens to a unit's registration once the developer receives the completion certificate?
questions.reference_answer: Sold units are entered in the Property Register in the name of purchasers who fulfilled their contractual obligations, once the department receives the completion certificate from the competent entities.

questions.question: What does Article 11 of Law 19 of 2017 allow a developer to do against a defaulting purchaser?
questions.reference_answer: It prescribes procedures and measures a developer may take against a defaulting purchaser without recourse to courts or arbitration, for off-plan sale agreements registered on the interim register.

questions.question: Under the escrow law, what must happen to payments made by off-plan purchasers?
questions.reference_answer: Payments by off-plan purchasers must be deposited into a project-specific escrow account dedicated exclusively to the construction of that development, under Law No. 8 of 2007.

questions.question: What penalty applies to someone conducting real estate development activity without a licence under the escrow law?
questions.reference_answer: A jail sentence and a fine of at least AED 100,000, or either penalty, applies to conducting real estate development activity without a licence.

questions.question: How is the Dubai residential house price index constructed methodologically?
questions.reference_answer: It uses a hedonic regression (hedonic imputation) methodology that treats housing as heterogeneous goods described by their attributes, producing monthly, quarterly and yearly indices.

questions.question: What period of Dubai real estate performance does the DLD Annual Report 2024 cover?
questions.reference_answer: It covers transaction volumes, price movements, investment behavior and market shifts from 2007 to 2024, with emphasis on 2023 and early 2024.

questions.question: Which factors most often make an early off-plan resale uneconomic?
questions.reference_answer: The developer assignment fee (around 2 to 5 percent of the original price) and the minimum payment threshold: a seller who has paid only a small share may be below threshold, and even if eligible the assignment fee can wipe out a thin premium.

questions.question: How does construction progress affect an off-plan unit's resale?
questions.reference_answer: Higher completion percentage generally lifts buyer confidence and price and also helps clear the minimum payment threshold, so progress affects both eligibility to sell and demand.

questions.question: What is the highest price per square foot among the off-plan resale listings sampled?
questions.reference_answer: Around AED 3,500 per square foot (a Palm Jumeirah / Business Bay apartment in the sampled listings).

questions.question: Name communities where off-plan resale apartments are listed in the sample.
questions.reference_answer: Communities include Dubai Islands, Business Bay, Dubai Marina, Palm Jumeirah, Dubai Creek Harbour, JLT, and Dubai Silicon Oasis.

questions.question: Who must facilitate an off-plan assignment sale and where is it finalized?
questions.reference_answer: It must be facilitated by a RERA-registered broker and finalized at a DLD-approved trustee office, with the Oqood record updated to the new buyer.

questions.question: What is the DLD transfer fee on an off-plan resale and who typically pays it?
questions.reference_answer: The DLD transfer fee is 4% of the sale price, typically paid by the buyer, though it can be split 2%/2% if agreed in the MOU.

questions.question: Why does developer reputation affect off-plan resale price?
questions.reference_answer: Tier-1 developers with a delivery track record command stronger resale demand and premiums, while weaker developers widen discounts.

questions.question: What must be true about a unit's Oqood registration before an assignment has legal standing with the DLD?
questions.reference_answer: The unit must be registered in the interim (Oqood) register and the Oqood record must be updated to name the new buyer; otherwise the transfer has no legal standing with the DLD.
